input.content:
name: Release

# A tag is the release: v1.5.0 builds the APKs, runs the same tests as the
# Android workflow, and publishes them as a GitHub release. The app reads
# /releases/latest to find out what is new, so publishing here is what makes an
# update show up on a phone.
#
# The APKs are named PocketRun-<tag>-release.apk / -debug.apk, which is what
# dev.pocketrun.update.AppUpdate looks for.

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: "Existing tag to publish (e.g. v1.5.0); empty = the pushed tag"
        required: false
        default: ""

permissions:
  contents: write

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    name: Build and publish
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 60
    env:
      TAG: ${{ inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.tag || github.ref }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          # versionCode/versionName come from the nearest tag, and a checkout of
          # a ref does not fetch tags even at depth 0.
          fetch-tags: true

      - uses: actions/setup-java@v5
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: "17"

      - name: JDK 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v5
        if: ${{ inputs.tag != '' }}
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: "17"

      # Chaquopy needs a build machine Python matching the app's major.minor.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"

      - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4

      - name: Cache Chaquopy downloads
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.chaquopy
            ~/.gradle/caches/modules-2
          key: chaquopy-${{ hashFiles('android/app/build.gradle.kts') }}
          restore-keys: chaquopy-

      - name: Unit tests
        working-directory: android
        run: ./gradlew --no-daemon :app:testDebugUnitTest

      - name: Python sandbox tests
        run: python3 -m unittest discover -s android/app/src/test/python -v

      - name: Assemble release APK
        env:
          KEYSTORE_B64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_B64 }}
          KEYSTORE_PASS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          KEY_PASS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        # No working-directory here on purpose: the keystore lands in android/
        # (the Gradle rootProject) and gradlew is invoked from android/.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${KEYSTORE_B64:-}" ]; then
            echo "::error title=no signing key::ANDROID_KEYSTORE_B64 is not configured; a release without a signature is not an update."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$KEYSTORE_B64" | base64 -d > android/keystore.jks
          cat > android/keystore.properties <<EOF
          storeFile=keystore.jks
          storePassword=$KEYSTORE_PASS
          keyAlias=$KEY_ALIAS
          keyPassword=$KEY_PASS
          EOF
          cd android && ./gradlew --no-daemon :app:assembleRelease :app:assembleDebug

      - name: Name the assets
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p dist
          cp android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/*.apk "dist/PocketRun-${TAG}-release.apk"
          cp android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/*.apk "dist/PocketRun-${TAG}-debug.apk"
          ls -la dist

      - name: Publish the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if gh release view "$TAG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "releasing $TAG (replacing the assets of an existing release)"
            gh release upload "$TAG" dist/*.apk --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$TAG" dist/*.apk \
              --title "PocketRun $TAG" \
              --generate-notes
          fi

      - name: Build report
        run: |
          echo "### PocketRun $TAG" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          ls -la dist >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

Shared license key and in-app updates

Two things stood between a published build and the people who want it: a
key to paste and a way to get the next version. Both are now part of the
build rather than of the user's day.

The license: android/license.pubkey is a new keypair and
android/shared-license.key is a pro/lifetime key signed by it, baked into
BuildConfig and tried before the activation screen. A published release is
usable by anyone who installs it. The seed is not in the repository
(license.key is ignored), so whoever holds it can still issue keys of their
own; SharedLicenseTest fails the build if the two files ever stop matching,
because that failure looks like nothing at all on a phone. The button to
deactivate only shows for a key that is not the shared one, since
deactivating it would be undone on the next launch.

Updates: dev.pocketrun.update reads /releases/latest, compares the release
tag with the version the build reports (both come from the same tag, so
there is nothing else to keep in sync), downloads the release APK through a
.part file and hands it to the system installer. Nothing is installed
without the user saying yes. A check runs quietly once a day on launch and
on the button in the Info tab; AppUpdate has no Android in it, so the
version arithmetic and the release parsing are unit-tested.

Tagging v* is now the release: release.yml runs the same tests, builds both
APKs with the signing key and publishes them as PocketRun-<tag>-release.apk,
which is the name the updater looks for. Tags no longer run android.yml -
that workflow would only repeat it.
MSG

@@ -0,0 +1,87 @@
+package dev.pocketrun.core
+
+import java.io.File
+import java.util.Locale
+
+/** One line that matched, with enough context to jump straight to it. */
+data class SearchHit(val file: File, val line: Int, val text: String) {
+    val path: String get() = file.path
+}
+
+/**
+ * grep over a project. The agent edits files behind the app's back all the time,
+ * so "where did that change land?" needs an answer that does not require the
+ * user to open every folder by hand.
+ *
+ * Deliberately bounded: binaries are skipped, huge files are skipped, and the
+ * number of hits is capped. A search on a phone has to end, and saying "first
+ * 500 matches" is better than hanging.
+ */
+object ContentSearch {
+    const val MAX_HITS = 500
+    const val MAX_FILES = 3_000
+    const val MAX_FILE_BYTES = 1_000_000L
+
+    fun search(
+        root: File,
+        query: String,
+        showHidden: Boolean = false,
+        regex: Boolean = false,
+        caseSensitive: Boolean = false,
+    ): List<SearchHit> {
+        val needle = query.trim()
+        if (needle.isEmpty() || !root.isDirectory) return emptyList()
+        val pattern = if (regex) {
+            runCatching {
+                Regex(
+                    needle,
+                    if (caseSensitive) emptySet() else setOf(RegexOption.IGNORE_CASE),
+                )
+            }.getOrNull() ?: return emptyList()
+        } else {
+            null
+        }
+        val hits = ArrayList<SearchHit>()
+        var seen = 0
+        val stack = ArrayDeque<File>()
+        stack.addLast(root)
+        while (stack.isNotEmpty() && seen < MAX_FILES && hits.size < MAX_HITS) {
+            val dir = stack.removeLast()
+            for (child in dir.listFiles().orEmpty()) {
+                if (seen >= MAX_FILES || hits.size >= MAX_HITS) break
+                if (child.isDirectory) {
+                    val skip = child.name in FileTree.SKIP_DIRS
+                    val hidden = FileTree.isHidden(child)
+                    if (showHidden || !skip && !hidden) stack.addLast(child)
+                    continue
+                }
+                if (!showHidden && FileTree.isHidden(child)) continue
+                seen++
+                if (child.length() > MAX_FILE_BYTES) continue
+                val text = FileText.read(child, MAX_FILE_BYTES) ?: continue
+                addHits(child, text, needle, pattern, caseSensitive, hits)
+            }
+        }
+        return hits
+    }
+
+    private fun addHits(
+        file: File,
+        text: String,
+        needle: String,
+        pattern: Regex?,
+        caseSensitive: Boolean,
+        out: MutableList<SearchHit>,
+    ) {
+        val haystack = if (caseSensitive) needle else needle.lowercase(Locale.ROOT)
+        var lineNo = 0
+        for (line in text.lineSequence()) {
+            lineNo++
+            val found = pattern?.containsMatchIn(line)
+                ?: if (caseSensitive) line.contains(needle) else line.lowercase(Locale.ROOT).contains(haystack)
+            if (!found) continue
+            out += SearchHit(file, lineNo, line.trim().take(240))
+            if (out.size >= MAX_HITS) return
+        }
+    }
+}

--- android/app/src/main/java/dev/pocketrun/core/FileHistory.kt	
+++ android/app/src/main/java/dev/pocketrun/core/FileHistory.kt	
@@ -0,0 +1,103 @@
+package dev.pocketrun.core
+
+import java.io.File
+import java.io.IOException
+
+/** One saved copy of a file, newest first when listed. */
+data class Version(
+    val file: File,
+    val stamp: Long,
+    val size: Long,
+    val project: String,
+) {
+    val label: String get() = file.name.substringAfter("__", file.name)
+}
+
+/**
+ * Versions of the files the user cares about, kept beside the projects.
+ *
+ * The agent edits files without asking first (it does ask, but the user can
+ * approve a patch they have not read carefully), and there is no undo anywhere
+ * else in the app. So before anything overwrites or deletes a file - a save in
+ * the editor, a write from the agent, a delete in the file manager - the old
+ * content is copied here, and the file manager offers to put it back.
+ *
+ * Layout: `.history/<project>/<mangled-relative-path>/<stamp>__<name>`.
+ */
+class FileHistory(private val root: File) {
+
+    /** Copies the current content aside. Returns the copy, or null when there is
+     *  nothing to keep (missing file) or the copy failed. */
+    fun snapshot(file: File, projectDir: File): Version? {
+        if (!file.isFile) return null
+        val dir = dirFor(file, projectDir)
+        val target = File(dir, "${stamp()}_${file.name.take(80)}")
+        return try {
+            file.copyTo(target, overwrite = false)
+            version(target, projectDir.name)
+        } catch (_: IOException) {
+            null
+        }
+    }
+
+    /** Every saved copy of this file, newest first. */
+    fun versionsOf(file: File, projectDir: File): List<Version> {
+        val dir = dirFor(file, projectDir)
+        val entries = dir.listFiles()?.filter { it.isFile } ?: return emptyList()
+        return entries
+            .map { version(it, projectDir.name) }
+            .sortedByDescending { it.stamp }
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Puts a saved copy back. The current content is snapshotted first, so
+     * "restore" is itself undoable.
+     */
+    fun restore(version: Version, target: File, projectDir: File): Boolean {
+        if (!version.file.isFile) return false
+        if (target.isFile) snapshot(target, projectDir)
+        return try {
+            target.parentFile?.mkdirs()
+            version.file.copyTo(target, overwrite = true)
+            true
+        } catch (_: IOException) {
+            false
+        }
+    }
+
+    fun deleteVersion(version: Version): Boolean = version.file.delete()
+
+    /** Keeps the newest [keep] copies so the history folder cannot grow forever. */
+    fun prune(file: File, projectDir: File, keep: Int = 20) {
+        versionsOf(file, projectDir).drop(keep).forEach { it.file.delete() }
+    }
+
+    private fun dirFor(file: File, projectDir: File): File =
+        File(File(root, FileOps.slug(projectDir.name)), key(file, projectDir)).apply { mkdirs() }
+
+    /** The relative path with separators encoded, so a folder and a file with the
+     *  same name can never land in the same history slot. */
+    private fun key(file: File, projectDir: File): String {
+        val relative = try {
+            file.absolutePath.removePrefix(projectDir.absolutePath).trimStart(File.separatorChar)
+        } catch (_: IllegalArgumentException) {
+            file.name
+        }
+        val encoded = relative.replace("%", "%25").replace(File.separatorChar, '~')
+        return encoded.ifEmpty { file.name }
+    }
+
+    private fun version(file: File, project: String): Version = Version(
+        file = file,
+        stamp = file.name.substringBefore("__").toLongOrNull() ?: 0L,
+        size = file.length(),
+        project = project,
+    )
+
+    private fun stamp(): String = String.format("%013d", System.currentTimeMillis())
+
+    companion object {

+package dev.pocketrun.core
+
+import java.io.File
+import java.util.Locale
+
+/**
+ * What a file is to the UI. The tree icon, the viewer, the filter chip and the
+ * "открыть" action all read this one classification, so a file can never open in
+ * the wrong viewer because two lists disagreed about its type.
+ */
+enum class FileKind(val title: String) {
+    FOLDER("Папка"),
+    CODE("Код"),
+    TEXT("Текст"),
+    IMAGE("Фото"),
+    AUDIO("Аудио"),
+    VIDEO("Видео"),
+    ARCHIVE("Архив"),
+    OTHER("Файл"),
+}
+
+/** One row of the tree. A flat list with a depth keeps LazyColumn cheap. */
+data class FileNode(
+    val file: File,
+    val depth: Int,
+    val kind: FileKind,
+    val size: Long,
+    val modified: Long,
+    val folders: Int = 0,
+    val files: Int = 0,
+) {
+    val name: String get() = file.name
+    val isFolder: Boolean get() = kind == FileKind.FOLDER
+}
+
+/** What the tree shows: a name substring, one kind, and whether dotfiles count. */
+data class TreeFilter(
+    val query: String = "",
+    val kind: FileKind? = null,
+    val showHidden: Boolean = false,
+) {
+    val isFiltering: Boolean get() = query.isNotBlank() || kind != null
+}
+
+/**
+ * The project folder as a tree. A project really is a directory on disk - the
+ * whole point of this file is that the app stopped pretending otherwise: every
+ * file is visible, every file is openable, and a change made by the agent shows
+ * up without the user pulling to refresh.
+ */
+object FileTree {
+    /**
+     * Directories that are noise in a tree but must still work on disk. Skipped
+     * unless the user asks for everything.
+     */
+    val SKIP_DIRS = setOf(
+        ".git", "node_modules", "__pycache__", ".venv", "venv", ".gradle", ".idea",
+        ".cxx", ".pytest_cache", ".mypy_cache", ".ruff_cache", ".ipynb_checkpoints",
+    )
+
+    const val MAX_DEPTH = 12
+    const val MAX_NODES = 2_000
+
+    private val NAMED_CODE = setOf(
+        "makefile", "dockerfile", "rakefile", "gemfile", "procfile", "justfile", "brewfile",
+    )
+
+    private val CODE_EXT = setOf(
+        "py", "pyw", "js", "mjs", "cjs", "ts", "tsx", "jsx", "java", "kt", "kts", "c", "h",
+        "cc", "cpp", "hpp", "cs", "go", "rs", "rb", "php", "sh", "bash", "zsh", "fish", "ps1",
+        "sql", "html", "htm", "css", "scss", "sass", "less", "vue", "svelte", "lua", "pl", "r",
+        "swift", "gradle", "cmake", "m", "proto", "ex", "exs", "erl", "clj", "groovy",
+    )
+
+    private val TEXT_EXT = setOf(
+        "txt", "md", "markdown", "rst", "adoc", "log", "csv", "tsv", "json", "jsonl", "yaml",
+        "yml", "toml", "ini", "cfg", "conf", "env", "properties", "xml", "srt", "vtt", "lock",
+    )
+
+    private val IMAGE_EXT = setOf(
+        "jpg", "jpeg", "png", "gif", "webp", "bmp", "heic", "heif", "avif", "svg", "ico",
+    )
+
+    private val AUDIO_EXT = setOf(
+        "mp3", "wav", "ogg", "oga", "m4a", "aac", "flac", "opus", "mid", "midi", "amr", "3ga",
+    )
+
+    private val VIDEO_EXT = setOf(
+        "mp4", "mkv", "webm", "avi", "mov", "mpg", "mpeg", "m4v", "3gp", "ts", "wmv", "flv",
+    )
+
+    private val ARCHIVE_EXT = setOf(
+        "zip", "tar", "gz", "tgz", "bz2", "xz", "7z", "rar", "jar", "apk", "deb", "rpm",
+    )
+
+    fun ext(file: File): String = file.extension.lowercase(Locale.ROOT)
+
+    fun kindOf(file: File): FileKind {
+        if (file.isDirectory) return FileKind.FOLDER
+        val name = file.name.lowercase(Locale.ROOT)
+        val ext = ext(file)
+        return when {
+            ext in CODE_EXT || name in NAMED_CODE -> FileKind.CODE
+            ext in TEXT_EXT -> FileKind.TEXT
+            ext in IMAGE_EXT -> FileKind.IMAGE
+            ext in AUDIO_EXT -> FileKind.AUDIO
+            ext in VIDEO_EXT -> FileKind.VIDEO
+            ext in ARCHIVE_EXT -> FileKind.ARCHIVE
+            else -> FileKind.OTHER
+        }
+    }
+
+    /** True for anything the editor or the content search may open as text. */
+    fun isTextual(kind: FileKind): Boolean = kind == FileKind.CODE || kind == FileKind.TEXT
+
+    fun isHidden(file: File): Boolean = file.name.startsWith(".")
+
+    private fun skip(file: File): Boolean = file.isDirectory && file.name in SKIP_DIRS
+
+    /**
+     * The tree, flattened for a lazy list.
+     *
+     * Without a filter this walks only what the user has expanded, so a project
+     * with thousands of files costs a directory listing per open folder. With a
+     * filter the whole tree is walked once, and a folder is kept when the filter
+     * matches it or anything inside it - that is what makes a search reveal a
+     * file that sits in a collapsed folder.
+     */
+    fun build(root: File, expanded: Set<String>, filter: TreeFilter): List<FileNode> {
+        if (!root.isDirectory) return emptyList()
+        if (!filter.isFiltering) return walk(root, 0, expanded, filter.showHidden)
+        val all = walk(root, 0, everythingExpanded = true, showHidden = filter.showHidden)
+        val keep = keepSet(root, all, filter)
+        return all.filter { it.file.absolutePath in keep }
+    }
+
+    private fun walk(
+        dir: File,
+        depth: Int,
+        expanded: Set<String> = emptySet(),
+        showHidden: Boolean = false,
+        everythingExpanded: Boolean = false,
+    ): List<FileNode> {
+        if (depth > MAX_DEPTH) return emptyList()
+        val out = ArrayList<FileNode>()
+        for (child in children(dir, showHidden)) {
+            if (out.size >= MAX_NODES) break
+            val kind = kindOf(child)
+            out += node(child, depth, kind)
+            if (kind != FileKind.FOLDER) continue
+            val open = everythingExpanded || child.absolutePath in expanded
+            if (open) out += walk(child, depth + 1, expanded, showHidden, everythingExpanded)
+        }
+        return out
+    }
+
+    private fun node(file: File, depth: Int, kind: FileKind): FileNode {
+        if (kind != FileKind.FOLDER) {
+            return FileNode(file, depth, kind, file.length(), file.lastModified())
+        }
+        val entries = file.listFiles()
+        return FileNode(
+            file = file,
+            depth = depth,
+            kind = kind,
+            size = 0,
+            modified = file.lastModified(),
+            folders = entries?.count { it.isDirectory } ?: 0,
+            files = entries?.count { !it.isDirectory } ?: 0,
+        )
+    }
+
+    private fun children(dir: File, showHidden: Boolean): List<File> {
+        val entries = dir.listFiles() ?: return emptyList()
+        return entries
+            .filter { (showHidden || !isHidden(it)) && (showHidden || !skip(it)) }
+            .sortedWith(compareBy({ if (it.isDirectory) 0 else 1 }, { it.name.lowercase(Locale.ROOT) }))
+    }
+
+    /** The matches themselves plus every folder on the way to the project root. */
+    private fun keepSet(root: File, all: List<FileNode>, filter: TreeFilter): Set<String> {
+        val query = filter.query.trim().lowercase(Locale.ROOT)
+        val keep = HashSet<String>()
+        for (node in all) {
+            if (node.isFolder) continue
+            val byName = query.isEmpty() || node.name.lowercase(Locale.ROOT).contains(query)
+            val byKind = filter.kind == null || node.kind == filter.kind
+            if (!byName || !byKind) continue
+            keep += node.file.absolutePath
+            var current = node.file.parentFile
+            while (current != null && current.absolutePath.length >= root.absolutePath.length) {
+                keep += current.absolutePath
+                if (current.absolutePath == root.absolutePath) break
+                current = current.parentFile
+            }
+        }
+        return keep
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * A cheap summary of the whole tree, used to notice that the agent, the
+     * editor or a file imported from the phone changed something while the app was
+     * looking at it. Names, sizes and mtimes only - no nodes are built, so it is
+     * safe to run every couple of seconds.
+     */
+    fun fingerprint(root: File): String {
+        if (!root.isDirectory) return "-"
+        var hash = 1125899906842597L
+        var count = 0
+        val stack = ArrayDeque<File>()
+        stack.addLast(root)
+        while (stack.isNotEmpty() && count < MAX_NODES) {
+            val dir = stack.removeLast()
+            for (child in dir.listFiles().orEmpty()) {
+                count++
+                if (child.isDirectory && child.name !in SKIP_DIRS) stack.addLast(child)
+                hash = hash * 31 + child.name.hashCode()
+                hash = hash * 31 + child.length()
+                hash = hash * 31 + child.lastModified()
+            }
+        }
+        return "$count:${java.lang.Long.toHexString(hash)}"
+    }
+}

Now I understand the state. Let me summarize the answers to "почему":

1. **"файлы не меняются когда аи их меняет"** — `refreshProjects()` is only called in `init`, `createProject()`, `deleteProject()`. Nothing watches the filesystem, so the card summary ("main.py · N строк") and the project list never refresh when the agent writes/deletes files. Also `loadScriptForMode()` reads main.py only when you switch to the project or change mode — the editor doesn't reload after the agent edits main.py. So a file changed by the agent stays stale in the editor too. That's a real bug, not just missing polish.

2. **"проект почему файл а не папка"** — it IS a folder on disk (`workspace/projects/<name>/`), but the UI presents it as a single file: the card shows only `main.py · N строк`, and the hint says "Проект — это папка с main.py". The editor is hardwired to exactly two files: `main.py` and `main.js` (`loadScriptForMode`, `saveScript`). So functionally the project *is* one file. That was the v1.0 scope.

3. **"без дерева файлов и фильтров"** — never built. `ProjectsScreen` is a flat `LazyColumn` of project cards; there's no file browser at all.

4. **"без собственного проводника ... текст аудио видео фото и другие"** — no file manager, no media preview, no import from the device.

5. **"и многое другое"** — vague; I should ask.

So this is a genuine feature request spanning: real folder semantics in the UI, a file tree, filters, a built-in file manager (create/rename/delete/move, import), and viewers for text/image/audio/video/other, plus live refresh.

This is a large body of work — easily 1500+ lines across new UI + state + watchers. I should not blindly start writing; I need to:
- Confirm the priority/scope (the user said "и многое другое" — I need to know what else).
- Propose an architecture and the order of work.

But also: the user is frustrated, and just telling them "what do you want?" is annoying. The best move: explain briefly the "почему" (it's my fault, it was scoped to a single file), then propose a concrete plan in phases, and start on phase 1 immediately (which is unambiguous and fixes the actual bug: live refresh + a real file tree for the project with filters), while asking about the one thing only they can decide: should the tree be a new tab or replace the "Проекты" list, and how should import from the device work (SAF picker?).

Actually, let me think about what's genuinely ambiguous and worth asking vs. what I can decide:

Decidable by me:
- Live refresh: a file watcher (WatchService) or a poll. On Android 8+, `FileObserver` is available (android.os.FileObserver, API 29+ reliable; WatchService via java.nio works too). Since minSdk 26, `FileObserver` is API 29+. `java.nio.file.WatchService` works on API 26+ (implemented on Android). Hmm, Android's WatchService support: `FileSystem.getFileSystem().newWatchService()` — Android has a LinuxWatchService implementation since API 26? That's a big scope. Let me plan the implementation carefully and work through it in phases, committing and pushing after each phase (with CI verification), since that's the established workflow.

Let me think about the architecture:

**Core: a file model + watcher**

New file: `dev/pocketrun/core/FileNode.kt` or `core/FileTree.kt`:
- `data class FileNode(val file: File, val depth: Int, val kind: Kind, val size: Long, val modified: Long)` with `Kind` enum: DIRECTORY, TEXT, CODE, IMAGE, AUDIO, VIDEO, ARCHIVE, OTHER.
- `fun classify(file: File): Kind` by extension.
- `fun buildTree(dir: File, filter: FileFilter, expanded: Set<String>): List<FileNode>` — walk and produce a flat list with depth (LazyColumn needs a flat list; use `items` with a flattened tree). Sorting: directories first, then by name.
- Skip hidden/service dirs by default: `.git`, `node_modules`, `__pycache__`, `.venv`, `.mypy_cache`, `.pytest_cache`, `.DS_Store`, `.idea`.
- Limits: max depth, max entries (to keep it snappy), max file size for text reading.

**Watcher: `core/ProjectWatcher.kt`**
- `android.os.FileObserver` on the project dir (recursive: FileObserver doesn't do recursive watches on all versions; on API 29+ `FileObserver(String, int)` with a directory path is NOT recursive). Options: recursive FileObserver (one per directory, added/removed dynamically) or a polling loop.
  - Polling: a background thread in the ViewModel that walks the project tree every 1.5s and compares a fingerprint (path + size + mtime). Simple, no API issues, works on API 26. Cost: a stat per file every 1.5s; for a project with hundreds of files that's fine (a few ms).
  - I'll go with polling + fingerprint. It's the most robust on Android, no deprecated API, and it also catches changes made by other processes/SAF imports. And the agent runs in the same app, so no need for inotify.
  - Only poll when the projects screen is visible? The ViewModel doesn't know. Keep it simple: poll while the ViewModel is alive (every 2s), it's cheap and makes the editor stay in sync too. Add a `distinctUntilChanged` on the fingerprint to avoid recompositions.
- Also: after a tool call in the agent (`OpenCodeTools` write/edit/apply_patch/bash), we could bump a "dirty" flag to refresh immediately instead of waiting 2s. Nice touch: the ViewModel can set a flag when the agent finishes a turn. Simpler: the poll interval is short enough. I'll add a `markDirty()` call in the agent loop after each tool execution to make it instant.

**State in AppViewModel:**
- `_tree: MutableStateFlow<List<FileNode>>`, `treeFilter`, `expandedDirs`, `selectedFile`.
- `fun refreshTree()`, `fun toggleDir(path)`, `fun setFilter(f)`, `fun setQuery(q)`, `fun createFile/dir`, `fun rename`, `fun delete`, `fun move`.
- `_editorFile: MutableStateFlow<File?>` — the file open in the editor; `openInEditor(file)`; `saveScript` writes to that file (keeping main.py/main.js defaults when nothing is opened).
- Disk-change detection for the open file: if the file's mtime/size changed and the editor has unsaved changes → `_fileChangedOnDisk` state → show a warning + "перезагрузить/сохранить поверх".
- `_contentHits: MutableStateFlow<List<ContentHit>>` for grep.
- Import: `_importRequest: MutableStateFlow<Intent?>`? Better: expose `fun importLauncher(): Intent` and `fun onImported(uri: Uri)`. The Composable uses `rememberLauncherForActivityResult(ActivityResultContracts.OpenMultipleDocuments())`. Need `ContentResolver` to copy the stream into the project dir. ViewModel has the app context.

- History: `core/FileHistory.kt` — before overwriting/deleting a file (editor save, agent write? agent writes bypass us...), copy the old content to `workspace/.history/<project>/<timestamp>__<name>`. Hmm, OpenCodeTools is constructed somewhere in AppViewModel — I'd pass a history object.

Build tree:
```kotlin
object FileTree {
    val SKIP_DIRS = setOf(".git", "node_modules", "__pycache__", ".venv", "venv", ".gradle", ".idea", ".cxx", ".pytest_cache", ".mypy_cache", "dist-info")
    const val MAX_DEPTH = 12
    const val MAX_ENTRIES = 5_000
    const val MAX_TEXT_BYTES = 1_500_000L

    fun kindOf(file: File): FileKind { ... }
    fun isHidden(file: File): Boolean = file.name.startsWith(".")

    fun build(root: File, expanded: Set<String>, filter: TreeFilter, maxDepth: Int = MAX_DEPTH): List<FileNode> {
        if (!root.isDirectory) return emptyList()
        val out = ArrayList<FileNode>()
        walk(root, 0, expanded, filter, out)
        return out
    }
    private fun walk(...) {
        if (out.size >= MAX_ENTRIES) return
        val children = dir.listFiles() ?: return
        val visible = children.filter { showHidden || (!isHidden(it) && it.name !in SKIP_DIRS) }
        val sorted = visible.sortedWith(compareBy({ if (it.isDirectory) 0 else 1 }, { it.name.lowercase(Locale.ROOT) }))
        for (child in sorted) {
            val kind = kindOf(child)
            if (filter.kind != null && kind != filter.kind && !child.isDirectory) continue  // folders always shown
            if (query.isNotEmpty() && !matches(child, query)) { if (child.isDirectory) walk? } ...
        }
    }
}
```

Query semantics: when a query is set, I want to show matching files AND their ancestor folders. Since the tree only recurses into *expanded* dirs, a search should reveal matches inside collapsed dirs — otherwise searching finds nothing unless the user expands everything. Approach: when `query.isNotEmpty()`, treat all dirs as expanded (walk the whole tree) and keep a node only if it matches or has a matching descendant. That requires two passes: collect matches first, then build the path set.

Cleaner implementation:
1. If query is empty → walk only expanded dirs, no filtering (except hidden + kind).
2. If query is not empty → walk everything (up to limits), collect matched files; compute the set of ancestor paths; then build the flat list with only those nodes, and force-expand the ancestors.

I'll implement `build` with an inner `collect(root)` that returns a flat list of all nodes (dirs expanded fully) and then a filter pass:
- `matches(node)`: name contains query (case-insensitive) for files; for dirs, true only if it has a descendant match (computed from the collected set).
- Content search is a separate explicit action (the user asked for grep by content) — the query in the tree is name-only, plus a separate "искать по содержимому" action. Good separation: name filter = tree, content search = results list with file:line.

Same descendant-based approach. Let me unify: build the full list of nodes (all dirs expanded) once, then filter by `predicate(node) or hasMatchingDescendant(node)`. Full walk on every poll (2s) for a project with a few hundred files: fine. For node_modules... skipped. OK, but full walk every 2s + filter → allocation churn. With 5k entries cap it's fine on a phone (a stat per entry). Hmm, 5k stats every 2s could be ~50-100ms on a slow phone. But projects usually have < 500 files. I'll cap MAX_ENTRIES at 2000 and keep the poll at 2s; plus a "fingerprint" walk (path|size|mtime only, no FileNode allocation) for change detection, which is cheap. And to be safe, the full tree rebuild only happens when the fingerprint changes OR the filter/expanded state changes. 

So: `fingerprint(root)` (cheap, no allocation of nodes) drives the rebuild. When the fingerprint is unchanged and the UI state is unchanged, we don't rebuild. When the user expands/collapses or changes the filter, we rebuild (a one-off walk). But careful: the fingerprint doesn't know about "expanded" — the rebuild uses the fingerprint as a "dirty" trigger. Now I have a good picture. Let me write the code. I'll start with the core (pure logic) files, which are testable on the JVM, then wire the ViewModel, then the UI.

Let me write `core/FileTree.kt` first. Keep it tight and well-documented in the existing style.

I need to be economical with output. Let me write the files.

File 1: `core/FileTree.kt` — kinds, nodes, filters, build, fingerprint.

```kotlin
package dev.pocketrun.core

import java.io.File
import java.util.Locale

/**
 * What a file is to the UI. The icon, the viewer, the filter chip and the icon in
 * the tree all follow this one classification, so a file never opens in the wrong
 * viewer because two lists disagreed about its type.
 */
enum class FileKind(val title: String) {
    FOLDER("Папка"),
    CODE("Код"),
    TEXT("Текст"),
    IMAGE("Фото"),
    AUDIO("Аудио"),
    VIDEO("Видео"),
    ARCHIVE("Архив"),
    OTHER("Файл"),
}

/** One row of the tree. A flat list with a depth keeps LazyColumn cheap. */
data class FileNode(
    val file: File,
    val depth: Int,
    val kind: FileKind,
    val size: Long,
    val modified: Long,
    val folders: Int = 0,
    val files: Int = 0,
) {
    val name: String get() = file.name
    val isFolder: Boolean get() = kind == FileKind.FOLDER
}

/** What the tree shows: a name substring, one kind, and whether dotfiles count. */
data class TreeFilter(
    val query: String = "",
    val kind: FileKind? = null,
    val showHidden: Boolean = false,
) {
    val isFiltering: Boolean get() = query.isNotBlank() || kind != null
}
```

Then the object with classification and build.

```kotlin
object FileTree {
    val SKIP_DIRS = setOf(".git", "node_modules", "__pycache__", ".venv", "venv", ".gradle", ".idea", ".cxx", ".pytest_cache", ".mypy_cache", ".ruff_cache", "dist-info", ".DS_Store")
    const val MAX_DEPTH = 12
    const val MAX_NODES = 2_000
    const val MAX_TEXT_BYTES = 2_000_000L

    private val CODE_EXT = setOf(...)
    private val TEXT_EXT = setOf(...)
    ...

    fun ext(file: File): String = file.extension.lowercase(Locale.ROOT)
    fun kindOf(file: File): FileKind {
        if (file.isDirectory) return FileKind.FOLDER
        val name = file.name.lowercase(Locale.ROOT)
        val ext = ext(file)
        return when {
            ext in CODE_EXT || name in NAMED_CODE -> FileKind.CODE
            ext in TEXT_EXT -> FileKind.TEXT
            ext in IMAGE_EXT -> FileKind.IMAGE
            ext in AUDIO_EXT -> FileKind.AUDIO
            ext in VIDEO_EXT -> FileKind.VIDEO
            ext in ARCHIVE_EXT -> FileKind.ARCHIVE
            else -> FileKind.OTHER
        }
    }

    fun isSkipped(file: File): Boolean = file.isDirectory && (file.name in SKIP_DIRS)
    fun isHidden(file: File): Boolean = file.name.startsWith(".")

    /**
     * The tree, flattened. Folders come first, then names case-insensitively, and
     * a folder is walked only when it is expanded - unless a filter is on, in
     * which case everything is walked once to find what matches and only the
     * folders on the way to a match are kept.
     */
    fun build(root: File, expanded: Set<String>, filter: TreeFilter): List<FileNode>
```

Implementation of build:

```kotlin
    fun build(root: File, expanded: Set<String>, filter: TreeFilter): List<FileNode> {
        if (!root.isDirectory) return emptyList()
        val everything = if (filter.isFiltering) collect(root, filter.showHidden) else null
        val keep = everything?.let { visibleOnly(it, filter) }
        return when {
            everything == null -> walk(root, 0, expanded, filter.showHidden, null)
            else -> everything.filter { keep.contains(it.file.absolutePath) }
        }
    }
```
where `collect` walks everything (depth-limited) and returns nodes with depth; `visibleOnly(nodes, filter)` computes the set of paths to keep: for each node, keep if it matches (query on name + kind) or any descendant matches. And the resulting flat list must preserve the collect order (which is a pre-order walk with folders first at each level) — but the "folders first" sort is applied per level during collect, so the pre-order list is already display order. However, when a filter is active, ancestors of matches must be shown even if not expanded — that's exactly what the keep-set gives.

Hmm, but there's a subtlety: with a filter active, showing a *collapsed* tree of just the matching paths is right.

`walk` (expandable mode):
```kotlin
    private fun walk(dir: File, depth: Int, expanded: Set<String>, showHidden: Boolean, limit: Int?): List<FileNode> {
        if (depth > MAX_DEPTH) return emptyList()
        val out = ArrayList<FileNode>()
        for (child in sortedChildren(dir, showHidden)) {
            if (out.size >= MAX_NODES) break
            val kind = kindOf(child)
            out += node(child, depth, kind)
            if (kind == FileKind.FOLDER && child.absolutePath in expanded) {
                out += walk(child, depth + 1, expanded, showHidden)
            }
        }
        return out
    }
```
`collect` = same but always recurses and caps.

`sortedChildren(dir, showHidden)`: `dir.listFiles()?.filter { (showHidden || !isHidden(it)) && !isSkipped(it) }?.sortedWith(compareBy({ if (it.isDirectory) 0 else 1 }, { it.name.lowercase(Locale.ROOT) }))`.

Hmm: when `showHidden` is false, should SKIP_DIRS be hidden? Yes, keep skipping them (they're not "hidden dotfiles" but noise; and the "скрытые" toggle should show dotfiles but not node_modules? I'll let the toggle reveal both — simpler and honest: `showHidden` reveals dotfiles AND skip dirs).

`node(child, depth, kind)`: size = if dir then 0 else child.length(); modified = child.lastModified(); folders/files counts for dirs = `child.listFiles()?.count { isDirectory }` etc. — that costs an extra listFiles per dir. For a dir, I need those counts for the label "3 папки · 12 файлов". It's one listFiles per *displayed* folder — acceptable. But careful: in the filter case, `collect` walks everything and would listFiles every dir. Acceptable (bounded by MAX_NODES).

Actually to keep the poll cheap, I could skip counts for unexpanded folders. Let me compute counts only when the folder is expanded (shown expanded) — no: the label is nice for collapsed too. Let me just count, with a cheap guard: only if `child.list()` returns non-null and size < 5000. Fine, keep simple: `listFiles()` and count.

Fingerprint:
```kotlin
    /**
     * A cheap summary of the tree, used to notice that the agent (or SAF, or the
     * editor) changed something while the app was looking at it. Only names,
     * sizes and mtimes - no allocation of nodes, so it is safe to run every
     * couple of seconds.
     */
    fun fingerprint(root: File): String {
        if (!root.isDirectory) return "-"
        var hash = 1125899906842597L
        var count = 0
        val stack = ArrayDeque<File>()
        stack.addLast(root)
        while (stack.isNotEmpty() && count < MAX_NODES) {
            val dir = stack.removeLast()
            for (child in dir.listFiles() ?: continue) {
                count++
                if (child.isDirectory) {
                    if (child.name !in SKIP_DIRS) stack.addLast(child)
                }
                hash = hash * 31 + child.name.hashCode()
                hash = hash * 31 + child.length()
                hash = hash * 31 + child.lastModified()
            }
        }
        return "$count:${hash.toString(16)}"
    }
```
Careful: `continue` inside `for` over `dir.listFiles() ?: continue` — `?:` with continue works in Kotlin? `val files = dir.listFiles() ?: continue` is valid inside a loop. Yes, `continue` as an expression is allowed in Kotlin (since 1.4? `break`/`continue` in elvis is allowed in while loops... Actually Kotlin allows `?: continue` inside a loop only as a statement — yes, this is idiomatic and works).

Also file size helpers and readText with binary detection → `FileText.kt` or inside FileTree. Let me put text reading in `core/FileText.kt` (used by editor, search, viewer).

File 2: `core/FileText.kt`
```kotlin
object FileText {
    const val MAX_BYTES = 2_000_000L
    fun looksBinary(file: File): Boolean   // NUL in first 8 KB
    fun read(file: File, maxBytes: Long = MAX_BYTES): String?   // null when binary/too big
    fun decode(bytes: ByteArray): String   // UTF-8 with replacement
    fun sizeOf(dir: File): Long
}
```

File 3: `core/FileOps.kt`
```kotlin
object FileOps {
    fun safeName(raw: String): String?      // null when the name cannot be used
    fun uniqueName(dir: File, name: String): File
    fun createFile(dir: File, name: String, template: String = ""): File
    fun createDir(dir: File, name: String): File
    fun rename(file: File, newName: String): File?   // null when the name is bad
```

Watcher: a dedicated single-thread executor + a loop:
```kotlin
private val watchExecutor = Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor { r -> Thread(r, "pocketrun-files").apply { isDaemon = true } }
@Volatile private var watching = false
private fun startWatching() {
    if (watching) return
    watching = true
    watchExecutor.execute {
        while (watching) {
            refreshTreeIfChanged()
            Thread.sleep(2000)
        }
    }
}
```
Careful: the loop must not spin forever after `onCleared` → `stopWatching()` sets watching=false. Also, one long-lived task on a single-thread executor: if the loop is running, other tasks submitted to that executor queue up forever → don't share it. I use `ioExecutor` for the real work and a dedicated thread for watching. Good, as written.

`refreshTreeIfChanged()`:
```kotlin
private fun refreshTreeIfChanged() {
    val dir = _selected.value?.dir
    if (dir == null) { if (_tree.value.isNotEmpty()) _tree.value = emptyList(); return }
    val print = FileTree.fingerprint(dir)
    if (print == treePrint) return
    treePrint = print
    _tree.value = FileTree.build(dir, _expanded.value, _filter.value)
}
```
But `_expanded`/`_filter` are StateFlows; the tree also needs rebuilding when they change. So:
```kotlin
fun toggleFolder(file: File) { _expanded.value = ...; rebuildTree() }
fun setTreeFilter(f: TreeFilter) { _filter.value = f; rebuildTree() }
private fun rebuildTree() {   // must be off the main thread
    val dir = _selected.value?.dir ?: run { _tree.value = emptyList(); return }
    treePrint = FileTree.fingerprint(dir)
    _tree.value = FileTree.build(dir, _expanded.value, _filter.value)
}
```
`rebuildTree()` from UI callbacks runs on the main thread — a directory walk on the main thread is exactly the StrictMode-flavoured mistake I made with the NPE. Let me route everything through `ioExecutor`:
```kotlin
private fun rebuildTreeAsync() { ioExecutor.execute { rebuildTree() } }
```
And mutations (create/rename/delete/move/import) run on ioExecutor too, then rebuild.

There's a subtlety: `_tree.value = ...` from a background thread is fine with StateFlow (it's thread-safe).
